planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring or fall into acidic, well-drained soil enriched with organic matter.

directions: Sweetheart Supreme is a Pericat hybrid azalea bred by Alphonse Pericat of Collingdale, Pennsylvania and introduced into the trade around 1940, bearing semi-double, hose-in-hose blush-pink blooms in early to midseason. It is as cold-hardy as Kurume azaleas despite having been originally selected for greenhouse forcing. Grow in part shade with consistent moisture and acidic, humus-rich soil, mulching to keep roots cool. Prune lightly after bloom to maintain a dense, rounded form.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring or fall into acidic, well-drained soil in filtered sun.

directions: Twenty Grand was shown as an unnamed Pericat seedling at the 1931 Philadelphia Flower Show and later named and introduced to the trade by hybridizer David Leach; it produces 2-inch semi-double, red-violet-pink flowers with salmon undertones in early to early-midseason. Hardy to 0 degrees F, it is tougher than many greenhouse-forcing Pericat siblings and suits open garden culture in zones 7 through 9. Site in filtered to full sun with evenly moist, acidic, well-drained soil, and shear lightly after flowering to keep its compact 3-by-3-foot habit tidy.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring or fall into acidic, well-drained soil in part shade.

directions: Hampton Beauty is a Pericat hybrid azalea prized for single, funnel-shaped deep-pink to vivid red blooms with a darker spotted blotch, opening in midseason on a dense, twiggy, mounding plant. Bred by Alphonse Pericat for greenhouse forcing, it proved as cold-hardy as the Kurume azaleas and reaches roughly 5 feet at 10 years in garden settings. Plant in part shade with acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil and keep evenly moist, especially through its first two seasons. Light post-bloom pruning keeps the naturally twiggy habit dense rather than leggy.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring or fall into acidic soil in shaded, rain-sheltered spots.

directions: Gardenia Supreme is a Pericat hybrid azalea, selected around 1930, noted for dense clusters of near-pure-white, lightly fragrant semi-double flowers resembling small gardenias against rich green foliage. It flowers mid to late spring on a dense, spreading shrub and performs best with some protection from heavy rain, which can bruise the delicate white petals. Grow in shaded to partly shaded sites with acidic, well-drained soil kept consistently moist, and avoid overhead watering during bloom. Light shaping after flowering maintains its naturally full, spreading form.
